title: Nuno Espirito Santo praises Maximilian Kilman response to West Ham boos
content:
Nuno Espirito Santo believes Maximilian Kilman “handled the situation well” after the defender was booed by sections of West Ham United’s fanbase during Sunday’s FA Cup quarter-final loss against Leeds United.

Kilman, who joined from Wolverhampton Wanderers for £40million in July 2024 on a seven-year contract, was jeered after conceding a penalty for a foul on Brenden Aaronson. It was Kilman’s first start since the fourth-round victory against League One side Burton Albion in February.

The 28-year-old centre-back had been an ever-present member of the team under Nuno before being dropped following the 3-0 loss to Wolves in January. When Jean-Clair Todibo sustained a calf injury in the warm-up before the 2-0 away loss to Aston Villa in March, Nuno replaced the defender with midfielder Freddie Potts and rejigged his formation, as opposed to making a like-for-like change with Kilman.

But ahead of West Ham’s crucial league game against Wolves on Friday, Nuno has come to Kilman’s defence.

“I saw a good game for Max,” said Nuno in Wednesday’s pre-match press conference. “There was the penalty but he handled the situation well, especially considering he did not play for such a long period. The team showed a lot of togetherness by supporting him. He’s fine (at the moment) and everyone goes through different moments. It’s about how you react and Max reacted well.

“I truly believe that the fans understand the situation, and the need for them is a lot. Sunday was a clear example that we as a group don’t give up, so I hope the fans support and back us on Friday.”

West Ham have not won a league game since beating Fulham in March. Nuno’s side are in the relegation zone, one point adrift of 17th-place Tottenham Hotspur. But if the east London side beat Wolves, Tottenham will drop into the bottom three for the first time this season.

West Ham were without Todibo, Crysencio Summerville, Callum Wilson and Konstantinos Mavropanos for the loss to Leeds, but Nuno is hopeful they will soon return to action.

“Summerville, Todibo and Wilson are improving,” the head coach added. “We still have tomorrow to assess them but we are positive that they can be available (against Wolves). Mavropanos is also clear of the concussion protocol (for a head injury he sustained while on international duty with Greece).

“We, as a club, are in a position we don’t want to be in. It’s up to us to take care of the mission. We are confident (about staying up) and we believe in each other.”
